subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a sketchbook in GCSE Art?
options: To record ideas and show development of work
questions.explain: A sketchbook records observations, experiments and the development of ideas towards a final piece.

options: A small preliminary model of a sculpture
questions.explain: A maquette is a small-scale model made to plan and test ideas for a larger sculpture.

options: Pouring liquid material into a mould to set into shape
questions.explain: Casting pours a liquid such as molten metal or plaster into a mould, where it hardens into the form.

options: Thick paint applied so brush or knife marks stand out
Paint thinned to a watery wash
Painting only in black and white
questions.explain: Impasto is thickly applied paint that leaves visible, textured marks on the surface.

questions.q: Etching is a printmaking process that uses what to cut into a metal plate?
questions.explain: In etching, acid bites into exposed lines of a metal plate, which then hold ink for printing.

options: A thin, transparent layer of diluted paint
Thick paint applied with a knife
questions.explain: A wash is a thin, transparent layer of watercolour spread over an area to build colour gradually.

questions.q: The sculpture technique of removing material from a solid block is called...
questions.explain: Carving is a subtractive method, cutting away material from a block of stone or wood.

questions.q: Which set lists the three primary colours?
questions.explain: In traditional art theory the primaries are red, yellow and blue, from which other colours are mixed.

questions.q: In one-point perspective, where do parallel lines appear to meet?
options: At a single vanishing point on the horizon
questions.explain: One-point perspective has receding lines converging at a single vanishing point on the horizon.

options: The arrangement of elements within an artwork
The size of the canvas only
questions.explain: Composition is how the visual elements are arranged and organised within the picture area.

questions.q: How are complementary colours defined on the colour wheel?
options: Colours that sit next to each other
Colours that sit directly opposite each other
Different tones of the same hue
questions.explain: Complementary colours are positioned opposite one another on the colour wheel, such as red and green.

questions.q: Which medium is a soft, powdery stick available in soft (chalk) or oil form?
questions.explain: Pastels are sticks of pigment, made as soft chalk pastels or richer oil pastels.
